title: CUSHMAH - Benefit of steroidogenesis inhibitors in Mild Cushing syndrome (Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion): a randomized trial in patients with Primary Bilateral Macronodular Adrenocortical Hyperplasia
official: CUSHMAH - Benefit of steroidogenesis inhibitors in Mild Cushing syndrome (Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion): a randomized trial in patients with Primary Bilateral Macronodular Adrenocortical Hyperplasia
summary: Main objective: Demonstrate that cortisol secretion inhibition by medical treatment (metyrapone) in PBMAH patients with MACS lead to improvement of hypertension and diabetes.
conditions: Primary Bilateral Macronodular Adrenal Hyperplasia causing moderate Cushing Syndrome (Mild autonomous Cortisol secretion)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years old
2. French speaking
3. Patient with PBMAH as determined by adrenal imaging (CT-scan and/or MRI) showing multiples bilateral supracentrimetric adrenal nodules
4. Mild autonomous cortisol secretion: plasma cortisol after 1 mg overnight dexamethasone test > 50 nmol/L, 24 h Urinary free cortisol < 1,5 upper limit of Normal
5. Adrenal origin of cortisol excess: morning plasma ACTH < 10 pg/ml or between 10 and 20 pg/ml non responsive to CRH stimulation (stimulation < 50 %)
6. Hypertension (systolic blood pressure > 140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure > 90 mmHg) or treated hypertension and/or diabetes that can be treated with antidiabetic treatments (WHO criteria)
7. For women of childbearing potential (WOCBP), negative bHCG and highly effective contraception
8. For male, an effective method of contraception
9. Signed a written informed consent
10. Affiliated to social security regime or an equivalent system
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients with a Cushing syndrome from another causes than PBMAH
2. Pregnancy or breastfeeding women
3. Steroidogenesis inhibitor treatment less than 6 weeks before inclusion
4. Pathology that is life-threatening in the short term (1 year)
5. Patients with major psychiatric disorders that may interfere with the smooth running of the study
6. Patients on AME (state medical aid)
7. Participation to another clinical trial on medicinal products for human use
8. Patients with proven primary adrenal insufficiency
9. Under glucocorticoid (systemic or high dose local) treatment
10. Contraindication to steroidogenesis inhibitor
11. Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to one of its excipients
12. Uncontrolled diabetes (HBA1c > 9 %)
13. Loop diuretics and thiazide or thiazide-like diuretic that can cause hypokaliemia
14. Patients at high risk of cardiac rhythm disorders with QT/QTc interval > 470ms (for women) and > 450ms (for men)
15. Drugs with a known risk of QT prolongation as listed in https://crediblemeds.org
